_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody; approved under accelerated approval based on response rate and durability of response.

pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label, multicenter, multicohort study of talquetamab monotherapy
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma; the primary efficacy population had received at least 4 prior lines of therapy including a PI, an IMiD, and an anti-CD38 mAb and were not exposed to prior T-cell redirection therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) assessed by an Independent Review Committee using IMWG 2016 criteria, supported by duration of response (DOR)
pivotal_trials.n: N=100 at 0.4 mg/kg weekly; N=87 at 0.8 mg/kg biweekly
pivotal_trials.result: 0.4 mg/kg weekly (n=100): ORR 73% (95% CI 63.2%, 81.4%), median DOR 9.5 months (95% CI 6.5, NE). 0.8 mg/kg biweekly (n=87): ORR 73.6% (95% CI 63.0%, 82.4%).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) include pyrexia, CRS, dysgeusia, nail disorder, musculoskeletal pain, skin disorder, rash, fatigue, weight decreased, dry mouth, xerosis, dysphagia, upper respiratory tract infection, diarrhea, hypotension, and headache. CRS occurred in 76% of patients (Grade 3 or 4 1.5%); neurologic toxicity including ICANS occurred in 55% (Grade 3 or 4 6%). Serious infections occurred in 16% with fatal infections in 1.5%.
target_moa: Talquetamab is a bispecific GPRC5D-directed CD3 T-cell engager: it binds CD3 on T cells and GPRC5D on multiple myeloma cells, resulting in T-cell activation and subsequent lysis of GPRC5D-expressing multiple myeloma cells.
modality: Bispecific antibody (humanized IgG4 GPRC5D x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager)

boxed_warning.content: Boxed Warning for Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), including life-threatening or fatal reactions, and Neurologic Toxicity, including immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), including serious and life-threatening or fatal reactions.

rems.type: TALVEY is available only through a restricted program called the TECVAYLI and TALVEY REMS because of the risks of CRS and neurologic toxicity, including ICANS.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee Meeting was not held; no external consults were requested.
